data.gender_notes: Khasibah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'khasasa' which means 'to give' or 'to provide'. In Islamic tradition, the name Khasibah is associated with those who are generous and giving, making them a source of blessings and joy for others. The name Khasibah carries the meaning “The Giver, Generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khasibah usually hope their child will grow to embody the giver, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Khasibah is also a name that is commonly given to both boys and girls, reflecting the gender neutrality and inclusivity of the Islamic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spiritual tradition, the name Khasibah is associated with the spiritual quality of being a constant giver. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "The believer's shade on the Day of Resurrection will be his charity," and giving, in any form, whether it be time, resources or kindness, is considered a means of seeking Allah's pleasure and a way to purify the heart. The name Khasibah serves as a reminder to be generous and giving, not only to others but also to ourselves and the world around us, and to strive towards being a source of blessings and joy for others.
